introduction.text: The Capitolium is a Roman temple located in Regio I of the Ostia archaeological area in Rome. It was the main temple of the city, dedicated to the Capitoline Triad.

history.description: The Capitolium was built in 120 AD during Emperor Hadrian's reign.
The temple was closed and abandoned after 394 AD when Christianity became the official religion of the Roman Empire.
The city was systematically destroyed from the 9th century onward, with the Capitolium remaining as one of the few visible remains.
Excavations in 1802-1804 identified the building as the temple of the Capitoline Triad.
In 1864, excavations uncovered four rooms beneath the podium.
The temple was converted into an ovile and called 'casa rossa' due to its brick construction.

design.description: The temple was a prostilo esastilo with six front columns, two on the pronaos, in Corinthian order.
It had a high podium with 21 steps, similar to the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on the Capitoline Hill.
The cella was rectangular, with three niches for the deities, and was covered in white and colored marble.
The interior rooms beneath the podium had opus spicatum flooring and were accessed by a rear door.
The temple was constructed in brick (laterite) and had a bronze entrance door.

art.description: The altar was covered in marble slabs decorated with reliefs of weapons.
The cella's marble panels were white and colored, with traces of the original arrangement.
The bronze entrance door was similar to those preserved at the Pantheon.
